programme: TP53 and TP73 form the core p53-family DNA-damage/apoptosis checkpoint (shared targets CDKN1A, MDM2, BAX, GADD45A, CCNE1); CARF (an ARF-pathway collaborator) and VHL feed into this checkpoint by stabilizing p53 activity and coupling it to HIF1A-driven hypoxia signaling; NFE2L2 (NRF2) supplies the parallel oxidative-stress arm that cross-talks with p53 stability; HMGA2 sits downstream/antagonistic to this checkpoint, suppressing p53-driven senescence and instead driving EMT-type transcription (SNAI1, TWIST1, VIM, CDH1 among its targets, overlapping VHL's EMT targets SNAI1/ZEB2/CDH1). Together these six factors form a p53/ARF-HIF-NRF2 stress-response module that decides between senescence/apoptosis and survival/proliferation under DNA-damage, hypoxic, or oxidative stress.
role_in_a: In Alzheimer's disease this axis governs the neuronal/glial response to chronic oxidative stress and proteostatic damage: VHL ubiquitinates APP and gates its lysosomal degradation and interacts with the HIF axis to modulate APOE4-driven pathology, NFE2L2 activity restrains tau seeding, and HMGA2 modulation (via PI3K/AKT) affects neuronal survival — i.e., the same checkpoint that elsewhere triggers apoptosis is instead tuned toward chronic stress-adaptation and senescence in post-mitotic neurons.
role_in_b: In ovarian cancer (especially HGSOC) this is the canonical tumor-suppressor/hypoxia-adaptation axis: TP53 mutation is near-universal and genome-defining, TP73 substitutes for lost p53 function and predicts platinum resistance and aggressive disease, CARF loss promotes tumorigenesis via the miR-451 axis, VHL-HIF machinery and NRF2 support hypoxic and redox adaptation and chemoresistance, and HMGA2 drives EMT-based metastasis — the same checkpoint here is disabled or subverted to permit survival and spread rather than triggering apoptosis.
shared_axis: Both diseases converge on the same p53/ARF-HIF-NRF2 stress-decision node, just with opposite outputs: tumor cells inactivate or repurpose it to escape apoptosis and adapt to hypoxia/oxidative stress, while stressed neurons chronically engage it toward senescence/death rather than proliferation, consistent with the epidemiologically observed inverse relationship between cancer and neurodegenerative disease risk.
reasoning: Five of the six carrying factors (TP53, VHL, NFE2L2, HMGA2, and to a lesser extent TP73) each have literature placing them mechanistically in both diseases, and TP53 has a review (41942427) explicitly spanning cancer and neurodegeneration, so the module is nameable and independently anchored, not manufactured from co-occurrence alone. It falls short of 'established' because no retrieved source states an AD-ovarian cancer link directly, one anchor paper for TP73 in AD is a negative/null finding (23414597), and CARF has no AD evidence at all, so the cross-disease connection still rests on the inverse-comorbidity reasoning rather than on retrieved fact.
support: PMID 34150043 — HMGA2 modulated via miR-132/PI3K-AKT in AD mouse model; PMID 39694080 — HMGA2 drives ovarian cancer metastasis via USP30/S100A6; PMID 41075454 — HMGA2-linked pseudogene targeting reduces ovarian tumor growth; PMID 23414597 — reports lack of TP73-AD association in mice/humans (negative evidence); PMID 40244040 — TP73 predicts platinum resistance in ovarian cancer; PMID 35867729 — TP73 as prognostic/predictive marker in ovarian cancer; PMID 41055405 — VHL ubiquitinates APP, governs lysosomal degradation (AD-relevant); PMID 39874294 — VHL-HIF axis suppresses APOE4-induced neuropathology; PMID 41061294 — VHL-pathway PROTACs suppress ovarian tumorigenicity; PMID 42353021 — TP53 as multi-target hub in AD systems-biology model; PMID 42180855 — TP53 mutation used for ctDNA monitoring in HGSOC; PMID 42444708 — natural compounds computationally targeting TP53 in ovarian cancer; PMID 41942427 — review connecting p53 biology across both cancer and neurodegeneration; PMID 41650822 — NRF2(NFE2L2) deficit alters tau seeding in tauopathy model; PMID 41702359 — NFE2L2-linked AKR1C inhibitors show ovarian antitumor activity; PMID 40935266 — NFE2L2 implicated in ovarian cancer risk analysis; PMID 29321561 — CARF suppression via miR-451 linked to tumorigenesis (ovarian-cancer relevant).
how_to_falsify: In parallel, knock down/inhibit VHL, NFE2L2, and HMGA2 in an APOE4 iPSC-neuron model and in an HGSOC cell line, then measure canonical p53/p73 target genes (CDKN1A, MDM2, BAX). The account predicts concordant activation of this checkpoint toward senescence/death in neurons but toward apoptotic sensitization (e.g., increased platinum sensitivity, given TP73's role in resistance) in the cancer cells; if perturbing these factors fails to move the same p53/p73 target set in both cell contexts, the claim of a single shared regulatory module is falsified.
caveats: Brain and ovary are anatomically and developmentally unrelated tissues, so any shared axis must be a generic stress-response circuit rather than a tissue-specific pathway; only 6 independent cohort pairs underlie the 128 patient-group comparisons, so the apparent recurrence has limited independent replication. TP73's AD evidence is a reported null result, not a positive link, and CARF and TEAD4/KAT7/PGR/GLIS3/CREM/IKZF4 (excluded from the module) either lack cross-disease evidence or don't cohere mechanistically with the p53/HIF/NRF2 axis — their exclusion reflects thin/off-target literature, not that the module is exhaustive. Tissue-generic exclusions (SOX10, ZEB1, NOTCH1, etc.) correctly remove likely confounding EMT/generic regulators, but ZEB1's absence from this account is a reason for humility about how much of the EMT-linked signal (via HMGA2/VHL) is tissue-generic rather than disease-specific.
